To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the spin-orbit coupling constant is different for neutrons and protons, (ii) the spin-orbitsplitting is different from the spin-orbit strength, and (iii) a new spin-orbit term, which is not present in the Skyrme functional, should be added to the HF potential.

i) the Skyrme HF model with pairing is a very good tool to study the evolution of the nuclear properties of the germanium and selenium chains; ii) the spin-orbit splitting in these nuclei cannot be properly described by existing parametrizations; iii) the spin-orbital splittings can be improved by using different spin-orbit constants for neutrons and protons, together with pairing; iv) the spin-orbits constants are not universal and depend on the nucleus.

the use of different spin-orbit coupling strengths for neutrons and protons in a constrained HF+BCS approach allows to reproduce the measured spectroscopic factors and the rms radii of the germanium and selenium isotope chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spin-orbit interaction and how it is described in nuclear energy density functional (EDF) theory.
the spin-orbit coupling in Skyrme energy functionals and its impact on the description of nuclear properties.

the development of new Skyrme paramatrizations that are able to describe spin-orbit effects in nuclei and the role played by the spin-orbit interaction in the description of the evolution of the nuclear landscape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spin-orbit splitting of single-particle levels is not a trivial property of a Skyrme interaction, but it requires the use of different coupling constants for neutrons and protons, as well as pairing and deformation.
the spin-orbit coupling in Skyrme functionals is not well understood yet and needs further study.
a spin-orbit coupling strength that depends on both the neutron and the proton number is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to obtain an improved description of the experimental data for the spin-orbit splitting of the valence states of the Ge and Se isotopes by introducing a new spin-orbit term in the HF potential.

, although Skyrme interactions have been used for many years in nuclear structure calculations, it is still possible to obtain new parametrizations that are better suited to describe nuclear properties.
, with the inclusion of pairing, deformation and the new spin-orbit coupling, we are able to obtain good results for the single-particle and collective properties of germanium isotopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin-orbit coupling constant of the Skyrme force can be different for neutrons and protons.
a simple modification of the spin-orbit coupling constant in the Skyrme energy functional can lead to a significant improvement of the description of single-particle properties in nuclei.
, in order to describe the spin-orbit splitting of the single-particle states, it is important to use a different spin-orbit coupling constant for neutrons and protons.
